A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 48 readable pages, including Appendices A-G. Full text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and synthetic data, including activation matching, interpolation barriers, and neuron swap costs in Section 6 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix G, including the transformer and subspace-coherence experiments.

M1.justification: The fixed-offset and masking parameterization, realization-cost framework, and alignment and interpolation procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MNIST, CIFAR-10, Gaussian-mixture, and synthetic coherence tasks. Appendix G retains the same additional evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Section 6 and Appendix G, including standard, W-asymmetric, syre, and activation-asymmetric models in their respective comparisons.

E3.justification: The data splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics, and evaluation procedures in Section 6 and Appendices F-G are identical.

E4.justification: The fixed-weight, sparsity, intrinsic-dimension, width, and coherence analyses are retained unchanged, as are the layerwise analyses and comparisons of realization-cost estimators.

E5.justification: Run counts and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including eight model pairs for Figure 4 and the 50-pair mean and standard deviation reporting described in Appendix F.5.

E6.justification: All reported results in Section 6 and Appendix G are identical. For example, Q3 retains accuracy drops of 46.4, 15.7, and 6.1 percentage points for intrinsic dimensions 2, 8, and 32.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theorems, and proofs are unchanged. The added Section 3.2 reference to relaxed assumptions points to Appendix E, whose complete analysis already appears identically in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about effective symmetry breaking, neuron identifiability, and unaligned linear mode connectivity.

C2.justification: The new Section 3.2 sentence summarizes the applicability beyond exact subspace support already explained in Appendix E. It introduces no new interpretation or limitation relative to the complete v1.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, data-processing instructions, and code-access information are unchanged, including Appendix F and the transformer setup in Appendix G.4.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 removes citations to Pope et al. (2021) and Ansuini et al. (2019) from the expectation of incoherent real-world inputs or representations. Both works remain cited elsewhere and in the bibliography; broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a brief pointer to Appendix E, and Section 4.1 loses a citation parenthesis. Apart from the updated version stamp, the language and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The edits cause small text shifts and changed line breaks across pages 3-5, alongside the updated first-page arXiv stamp. Figures, tables, captions, and their numbering are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing relaxed-assumption analysis easier to locate, but Appendix E already contained the same explanation and proofs in v1. The localized citation removal and text reflow leave the scientific evidence, reproducibility, and substantive exposition unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
